evidence: All three scored dimensions (aggregation weighted_mean) tell the judge to score each criterion on its own and continue after a failure. None contains stop-at-first-failure wording. functional/prompt.md L55-57: 'Score each criterion independently and continue after any failure; return a verdict for every criterion.' L23-25: 'Never carry a verdict across criteria ... when budget runs out, mark the rest failed and say so.' L29: 'Two failed attempts at the same control fail that criterion; continue.' L9: 'that criterion fails and scores 0; report what you saw and move on to the next criterion.' functional/judge.toml L6 mode='individual', so each criterion is also graded in its own session, which separates them structurally. polish/prompt.md L20-26 '## Independent scoring': 'One failed criterion does not zero the others. If a criterion cannot be performed, mark it failed and continue to every remaining criterion ... The global browser gate is the only all-or-nothing rule.' visual/prompt.md L38-43: the same text, using the 0 anchor. The only all-or-nothing rule is the in-dimension global browser gate (functional L11-19, polish L10-18, visual L18-26). The workbook allows this, and row 29 requires it. Gate dimensions render and constraints use aggregation all_pass, so they are exempt under the workbook text. I searched every scored prompt, judge.toml criterion, app_context.md and the gate prompts for stop, abort, halt, skip, 'first failure' and 'if X fails then others' wording. There are no hits that couple criteria. The persistence criterion (functional judge.toml L267-268) explicitly says it grades only durability, and that a feature which did not work before the restart is graded in its own criterion. That prevents a cascade from earlier features into persistence. Compared with the template: the task's independence wording keeps or strengthens every template statement (template functional L68-69, polish L14-20, visual L44-49). test.sh and tools/score.py are byte-identical to the template, so no scoring code was changed to break per-criterion independence. Adversarial check 1: an app that fails one functional criterion, for example a broken hold, still earns the weighted credit of the other 15 criteria under the prompt rules and individual mode. Nothing tells the judge to zero the rest. Adversarial check 2: a conforming app cannot lose unrelated criteria through prompt wording, because the only cross-criterion zeroing is the global gate, which a working app passes. Residual note, outside this row's wording scope (rows 28 and 37): the functional criteria share one database in a fixed order. A broken earlier write could therefore leave state behind that affects a later criterion, for example a wall on Dev for M-13 that wall_added_live failed to lift, which unread_and_new_messages_line then hits. That is state coupling, not prompt wording that stops scoring, and it penalizes only a genuinely broken feature. No configured judge run exists (raw-evidence-index scope says so). This row is decided by the prompt wording, not by a measurement, so its pass needs no runtime evidence. Whether the judge actually behaves this way remains unmeasured and is owned by the full-run rows.
